summary.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9% to a 47.6% margin, but Q4 ARPU of Rs.252 was dragged by roaming and 5G pack dynamics.
summary.overview: This is a combined Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom Q4 FY26 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) earnings webinar, held May 14, 2026, with the Hexacom segment covered in the second half. Hexacom delivered record FY26 net adds of 395,000 and a 3.4-point margin expansion to 47.6%, while Q4 revenue rose 2.3% sequentially to Rs.2,414 crore. Q4 ARPU was Rs.252 (about Rs.257-258 on an EDB basis) and management acknowledged headwinds from lower international roaming, handset price increases and 5G pack adoption. The Board recommended a Rs.18 dividend per share versus Rs.10 last year. A parent-level Africa share swap (additional 16.3% stake in Airtel Africa) was also announced, though it does not directly affect Hexacom.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex)

financial_highlights.value: Rs.252 reported; about Rs.257-258 EDB basis

segments.name: Mobile (Hexacom)
segments.commentary: Ended Q4 with 28.8 million mobile customers and about 370,000 net adds; ARPU of Rs.252 reported, held back by two fewer days, lower international roaming, handset price rises and 2G-to-4G upgrade pressure. Management said FY26 revenue growth was 8.3% against about 12% at Airtel, and the ARPU gap has narrowed.

segments.name: Homes and offices (Hexacom)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 51% with record net adds of 395,000 for the year; Q4 added a record 148,000 with revenue up about 21% QoQ. Growth is driven by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and the IPTV rollout.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said Hexacom is not lagging the market and will look for ways to grow faster.
Dividend payout is to rise progressively; Rs.18 per share recommended for FY26 versus Rs.10 last year.
Capex in Q4 was described as on plan; management said 5G densification will be funded if needed, with capex not being chased against a target.
Management expects smartphone upgrades to face some stress, which may leave Hexacom slightly behind on mobile growth.
Management said it will not give up on home acquisition and that FWA and fiber will both continue to be used where economical.
capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 capex Rs.586 crore, described as running as planned.
FY26 capex directed to 5G densification, network modernization and rapid growth of homes and IPTV.
Hexacom funds its own mobile and FTTH capex and does not participate in parent-level growth engines (data centres, cloud, financial services).
demand_pricing: Q4 ARPU headwinds: lower international roaming, handset prices rising (slowing 2G-to-4G upgrades), and 5G unlimited packs that break the price ladder.
Homes: FWA cost to connect has risen with chipset and memory prices; management says it will pivot to fiber where available, with the pivot slower in difficult terrains such as the north-east.
Competition: management described the market as competitive but said Hexacom is not lagging it.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Hexacom mobile revenue (8.3%) and EBITDA growth lagged Airtel, and should the gap close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hexacom is under-penetrated and the ARPU gap has narrowed; postpaid and international roaming mix will differ, and smartphone upgrades may stress growth. It is not lagging the market.

qa_highlights.question: Should Hexacom pay out a higher share of its cash flow, given it funds only mobile and FTTH?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that parent growth engines are not available to Hexacom, which limits new growth; dividend payout has moved from Rs.3-4 to Rs.10-18 per share and will keep rising progressively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the chipset shortage slow Hexacom's home growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of connecting homes is higher in difficult terrain and FWA lets it reach more homes; it will not give up acquisition and will prefer fiber where available.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU weakness only roaming-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5G pack adoption (eat-as-much-as-you-can packs) is a headwind alongside lower roaming and handset prices; Q4 ARPU is an average, with no red flag on the exit rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new regulatory charge this quarter and is there new government demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a prudent provision on an existing item where the interpretation changed; nothing new or exceptional, though the amount was not specified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the homes subscriber addition pace continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance but said there is no reason to expect a slowdown and the effort to grow homes continues despite competition.

risks_watch: Handset and chipset price increases could slow FWA and feature-phone-to-smartphone upgrades, weighing on mobile ARPU and homes growth.
Management flagged a regulatory-related provision this quarter; its size and recurrence are not disclosed.
Mobile growth gap versus Airtel (8.3% vs about 12% revenue growth in FY26) and the rate at which ARPU closes it.
Lower international roaming revenue and geopolitical effects (energy prices, gas for galvanizing) on tower build-outs and capex.
Finance cost stickiness at the parent level and the unwinding of one-off items in Africa.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating leverage and homes momentum, but candid that ARPU came in below expectations and that handset prices and roaming are headwinds. Answers on competition and forward-looking items were deliberately non-committal; management gave no guidance.
key_quotes: Our homes business continues to see strong momentum with record high net ads of 148,000, driving a revenue growth of about 21% sequentially.
I would say it is competitive, it is not lagging the market and we continue to look at opportunities as to how to grow faster.
We do not give guidance but see, the objective is to continue to grow.
There is nothing new, exceptional or unearthly which has come. It is just interpretation of issues as time progresses.

growth.why: No formal guidance was given; management said Hexacom is not lagging the market and will seek faster growth, with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified behind it.
